questions.q: The correct sequence of steps in a single machine cycle is:
questions.solution: The CPU first Fetches the instruction from memory, Decodes it in the control unit, Executes it in the ALU, and Stores the result.
questions.shortcut: Fat Dogs Eat Snacks: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store. Any option starting with Decode/Execute is out.

questions.q: A **pen drive** stores data on —
questions.solution: Pen drives (and memory cards, SSDs) use **flash memory** — non-volatile chips that keep data without power.
questions.shortcut: Pen drive = flash in your pocket.

questions.q: A hardware or software barrier that filters traffic between your network and the Internet by rules is a —
questions.solution: **Firewall** = the rule-based doorman of a network.

questions.q: To move to the next worksheet of a workbook, press —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+Page Down / Page Up** walk through the sheet tabs; Ctrl+arrows move within the data.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.

**P:** Children attend storytelling sessions there on weekends. **Q:** Libraries were once places only for silent reading. **R:** Adults, too, use their free computers to apply for jobs. **S:** Many have now become busy community centres.
questions.solution: **Q** is the only independent sentence. **S**'s 'Many' refers to the libraries and 'now' contrasts with 'once'. **P**'s 'there' needs the centres. **R**'s 'too' adds a second group, so it follows the children. **QSPR**.
questions.shortcut: Independent sentence first; 'too' marks the second of two examples.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** A new girl, Meena, joined our class in July. **P:** She had come from a village school that had just twenty students. **Q:** The two soon became inseparable friends. **R:** Our class teacher then asked Anu, the monitor, to help her settle in. **S:** Such a large class made her so nervous that she hardly spoke. **6.** Today Meena is one of the most popular students in school.
questions.solution: 'She' in **P** = Meena from S1. **S**'s 'Such a large class' contrasts with the twenty students in **P**, so the two form a pair. **R**'s 'then' is the teacher's response to her nervousness. **Q**'s 'The two' needs both Meena and Anu, so it follows **R**. **PSRQ**.
questions.shortcut: 'The two' needs both names; 'Such a large class' needs the twenty students.

questions.q:
Pick the odd sentence.

**A.** Sundarban mangroves absorb the first punch of Bay of Bengal cyclones. **B.** Their tangled roots trap silt and actually raise the land. **C.** Fishermen shelter in creek channels when warnings sound. **D.** The Thar desert's thorn forests need almost no rainfall. **E.** Plantation drives replant mangrove saplings after every storm.
questions.solution: A, B, C, E all work the mangrove theme; D is a different ecosystem entirely.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

He waited for / a hour at the bus stop / before he finally / took an autorickshaw.
options: a hour at the bus stop
questions.solution: *hour* begins with a silent *h*, so it starts with a vowel sound: **an hour**. *an autorickshaw* is correct.

questions.q: How many **moles** are there in **36 g of water**? (H₂O = 18 g/mol)
questions.solution: Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 36 ÷ 18 = **2 moles**.

questions.q: A traveller flying **east across the International Date Line** (from Asia towards America) must:
options: Add one day to the date
questions.solution: Across the IDL: going **east, lose a day**; going west (towards Asia), add a day. The line bends around islands so that no country is split into two dates.

questions.q: The Palk Strait separates India from:
questions.solution: The **Palk Strait** lies between Tamil Nadu and northern **Sri Lanka**; the Gulf of Mannar lies to its south, with Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) between them.

questions.q: An adult human skeleton has how many bones?
questions.solution: **206** in an adult; a newborn starts near 300 and many fuse as it grows. Ribs add 12 pairs to the count.

questions.q: The median of a data set is 9. Every value is increased by 3. The new median is:
questions.solution: Adding 3 shifts every value: median $= 9 + 3 = 12$.
questions.shortcut: Shifts translate the middle position too.

questions.q: Find the value of $1 \div \left(1 + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{2}}}\right)$
questions.shortcut: The whole $1 + \frac{1}{\dots}$ block sits under the first division.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks a bag at ₹750 and sells it for ₹600. The discount per cent is:
questions.shortcut: 25% treats ₹750 as a cost price — ₹600 is 80% of the tag price.

questions.q: What sum of money today is equivalent to ₹1,331 payable 3 years from now, compound interest being 10% per annum?
questions.shortcut: ₹1,210 uses $1.1^2$ — three years need three chips.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**LEVEL, RADAR, CIVIC, MOTOR**
questions.solution: LEVEL, RADAR and CIVIC read the same from both ends (**palindromes**). MOTOR read backwards is ROTOM → **MOTOR**.
questions.shortcut: Compare first and last letters: M ≠ R ends it at once.

questions.q: If **a ● b = a × b** when both a and b are even, and **a ● b = a + b** otherwise, find **(4 ● 6) + (3 ● 8)**.
questions.solution: 4 ● 6: both even → 4 × 6 = 24. 3 ● 8: 3 is odd → 3 + 8 = 11. Total = 24 + 11 = **35**. (48 multiplies both pairs.)
questions.shortcut: Test the condition for each pair separately.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Cracks have appeared in a bridge that was built only two years ago.

**Courses of action:**
I. Heavy vehicles should not be allowed on the bridge until engineers check it.
II. An inquiry should be held into the construction and action taken against those found responsible.
III. The state should stop building new bridges.

Which of the courses of action follow(s)?
options: All of I, II and III follow
questions.solution: I is an immediate safety step — **follows**. II finds the cause and fixes responsibility — **follows**. III is a sweeping reaction to one bridge's defect — **does not follow**. Answer: **only I and II**.
questions.shortcut: Safety now + inquiry follows; a blanket stop does not.

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**4, 10, 28, 82, 244, ?**
questions.shortcut: Ratio ≈ 3 with a left-over of −2 every step.
